verdict.executiveSummary149: Although Zhejiang [REDACTED] Knitting Co., Ltd. appears on paper to be a 25-year-old manufacturer (founded 2001, 10M RMB paid-in capital, customs exporter since 2003), Chinese public registry and judicial records reveal severe distress. The entity filed an active simplified deregistration notice (November 6–26, 2026), reported 0 insured employees in 2025 with all 3 branches cancelled, carries a 40.5M RMB resumed court enforcement case and 5 historical administrative penalties, and has closed both its Alibaba.com and 1688 storefronts while leaving its website unmaintained. Buyers should NOT sign contracts or wire funds to this entity.
verdict.executiveSummary249: On the surface, Zhejiang [REDACTED] Knitting Co., Ltd. displays the credentials of an established tier-2 knitwear manufacturer: founded in 2001, 10M RMB paid-in capital, 58 historical patents, 30 trademarks, and co-drafter of Chinese national knitwear standards. However, multi-source desk due diligence uncovers an acute 'winding-down legacy shell' profile: (1) an active simplified deregistration notice (Nov 6–26, 2026); (2) 0 insured employees across 2024 and 2025 annual reports with all 3 branches cancelled; (3) 40.5M RMB in resumed court enforcement (Jul 2025), 83.1M RMB in active chattel mortgages, 65.27M RMB in historical dishonest debtor orders, and 7 labor arbitrations; (4) all 3 recent ISO certificates revoked and all 58 patents terminated for unpaid fees; and (5) 6 active related entities sharing identical phone/email records—including 3 newly registered 2022–2024 trading/printing shells. Recommendation: Pause all payments immediately and verify whichever active successor entity the supplier proposes as counterparty.

practicalSafeguards: Do NOT sign a purchase contract or wire any deposit to this legacy legal entity while its simplified deregistration notice and 40.5M RMB enforcement remain unresolved.

Request a watermarked copy of the stamped Chinese Business License ('For supplier onboarding only') from whichever active entity the sales rep proposes as your counterparty—and verify that new entity before proceeding.

Require a formally stamped Proforma Invoice (PI). If the supplier requests USD payment to a Hong Kong or third-party export account, require a 1-page stamped Payment Authorization Letter signed by the contracting mainland entity.

Only if the active successor entity claims ISO 9001 or target-market test reports (e.g., OEKO-TEX / CPSIA), request scanned copies to verify that the certificate holder name matches the contracting entity and is still valid.

Before any bulk deposit to a newly verified successor factory, conduct a 5-minute live video walkthrough of the sample room/workshop and schedule third-party pre-shipment QC (e.g., SGS / TÜV) for production orders.
rfqQuestions: Public Chinese registry records show Zhejiang [REDACTED] Knitting Co., Ltd. filed a simplified deregistration notice in November 2026—which active legal entity will actually sign our contract and manufacture our order?

We noticed all three of the legacy factory's ISO certificates show status 'Revoked' and annual-report insured headcount is zero. Are you currently producing in-house under a successor company (such as Yiwu [REDACTED] Printing Co., Ltd.) or subcontracting to a partner workshop?
Will the beneficiary on our Proforma Invoice match the active contracting Chinese entity, or if using a Hong Kong account, can the mainland entity issue a stamped Payment Authorization Letter?
Can we arrange a 5-minute live video call from the production floor and confirm the exact factory address for third-party pre-shipment QC?
